fields.Front: What scope questions should you clarify before designing an Elevator System?
fields.Back: How many elevators and floors? A single bank or multiple? What dispatch/scheduling behavior is expected (nearest car, SCAN)? Capacity limits per car? Are requests external (hall calls) and/or internal (floor selection)?

fields.Front: What is the primary functional requirement of an Elevator System design?
fields.Back: Accept up/down pickup requests from floors and destination requests from inside a car, then dispatch/move the optimal elevator to serve each request efficiently.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the ElevatorController class?
fields.Back: Manages all elevator cars in the system, receives external and internal requests, and dispatches the best car to serve each request.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of the Elevator (car) class?
fields.Back: Tracks its own current floor, direction, and state (idle/moving); maintains its internal destination queue and moves toward requested floors.

fields.Front: What is the responsibility of a Request (hall call) class?
fields.Back: Represents a single pickup request — a floor plus a desired direction — waiting to be served by an assigned elevator.

fields.Front: What enum represents an elevator's direction of travel in this design?
What enum represents an elevator car's operational status?
Is the relationship between ElevatorController and Elevator composition or aggregation, and why?
fields.Back: Composition — the controller owns and manages the full lifecycle of its elevator cars; they don't exist independently of the system.

fields.Front: How should different dispatch algorithms (nearest-car, SCAN/look) be represented in the class design?
fields.Back: As interchangeable implementations of a common SchedulingStrategy interface, injected into ElevatorController rather than hardcoded.

fields.Front: Which design pattern fits swapping the elevator dispatch/scheduling algorithm, and why?
fields.Back: Strategy — each algorithm (nearest-car, SCAN) implements a common interface, so the controller can select or switch policy without changing its own code.

fields.Front: Which design pattern fits an elevator car behaving differently depending on whether it's Idle, Moving, or in Maintenance, and why?
fields.Back: State — encapsulate each mode's behavior in its own class, avoiding large conditionals scattered across Elevator's methods.

fields.Front: What are the two main entry-point APIs on ElevatorController?
fields.Back: requestElevator(floor, direction) for an external hall call, and selectFloor(elevatorId, floor) for an internal destination request.

fields.Front: What should Elevator.step() do on each tick of the simulation?
fields.Back: Move one floor toward its next destination, update its current floor and direction, and open its doors if it has arrived at a requested stop.

fields.Front: Tricky edge case: two hall calls request opposite directions from the same floor at the same time — how should this be handled?
fields.Back: Treat them as two independent hall calls; the dispatcher assigns cars based on each car's current direction and position — an up-call should not be served by a car already moving down past that floor.

fields.Front: Tricky edge case: the nearest elevator to a hall call is already at full capacity — what should the dispatcher do?
fields.Back: Exclude full cars from dispatch consideration (or have the car skip the stop) and assign/queue the request to the next available car instead.

fields.Front: Code an Elevator class in Python with current_floor, direction, and a method to add a destination and move one step.
fields.Back:
class Elevator:
    def __init__(self, id, current_floor=1):
        self.id = id
        self.current_floor = current_floor
        self.direction = "IDLE"
        self.destinations = set()

    def add_destination(self, floor):
        self.destinations.add(floor)
        if floor > self.current_floor:
            self.direction = "UP"
        elif floor < self.current_floor:
            self.direction = "DOWN"

    def step(self):
        if not self.destinations:
            self.direction = "IDLE"
            return
        if self.direction == "UP":
            self.current_floor += 1
        elif self.direction == "DOWN":
            self.current_floor -= 1
        if self.current_floor in self.destinations:
            self.destinations.remove(self.current_floor)

fields.Front: Code a nearest-idle-car dispatch method in Java: given a list of elevators and a requested floor, return the closest idle elevator.
fields.Back:
public Elevator findNearestIdleElevator(List<Elevator> elevators, int requestedFloor) {
    Elevator best = null;
    int bestDistance = Integer.MAX_VALUE;

    for (Elevator elevator : elevators) {
        if (elevator.getStatus() != ElevatorStatus.IDLE) {
            continue;
        }
        int distance = Math.abs(elevator.getCurrentFloor() - requestedFloor);
        if (distance < bestDistance) {
            bestDistance = distance;
            best = elevator;
        }
    }
    return best;
}

fields.Front: Code a simple State pattern in Python for an elevator's Idle/Moving states, each with a handle_request method.
fields.Back:
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

class ElevatorState(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def handle_request(self, elevator, floor):
        ...

class IdleState(ElevatorState):
    def handle_request(self, elevator, floor):
        elevator.add_destination(floor)
        elevator.state = MovingState()

class MovingState(ElevatorState):
    def handle_request(self, elevator, floor):
        elevator.add_destination(floor)
